mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate above 8% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate exceeds 8% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises and employment levels fall simultaneously, it indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate by 0.5% indicates tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate increases by 0.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPIAUCSL leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to decreased consumer spending.
failure_condition: If inflation is high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) increase, it indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both indicators increase but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts slow in late-cycle but S&P 500 returns are positive.
